comment: Inputs for build_stock.py. Curve/spectrum entries are points CSVs relative to tools/digitize/. midGreyLogExposure: the 'Camera Stops 0' tick (x = 445.9 pt) on the 7219 sensitometric graph lines up with log E -1.50 on the top LOG EXPOSURE axis calibrated by its frame-edge labels -4.0 and 1.0 (0 stops is exactly mid-frame). Reading the irregular local top ticks (-2.0 at 425.5, -1.0 at 462.0 pt) instead gives -1.44; see figures/7219_sensitometry.json.

sources.title: KODAK VISION3 500T Color Negative Film 5219 / 7219 / SO-219, Technical Data H-1-5219t (Revised 7-15)

BASE (7219 datasheet p.1): 'KODAK VISION3 500T Color Negative Films 5219 and 7219 have an acetate safety base with rem-jet backing'. ASSUMPTION: base thickness 0.127 mm (5 mil); the datasheet gives no thickness.
sources.note: Acetate base with rem-jet is datasheet fact; 0.127 mm is assumed (Britannica gives 0.08-0.2 mm as the typical photographic base range).

sources.title: ASSUMPTION: reflectanceOff 0.29 = diffuse internal reflectance of a base/air interface, 1 - (1 - 0.092)/n^2 with n = 1.48 (cellulose triacetate), about 0.585, times an assumed 0.5 ratio of red light reaching the base to red light absorbed in the emulsion.
sources.note: No published rem-jet-off reflectance was found. Searches (halation literature, Kodak AHU talking points) describe the mechanism only: rem-jet absorbs light before it reflects off the rear base surface.

sources.title: ASSUMPTION: reflectanceOn 0.01 (carbon-black rem-jet leaves about 1 % of the light returned).
sources.note: 'On' is the as-shipped state: the 7219 datasheet p.1 BASE section states the stock has rem-jet backing. The 1 % figure is assumed.

sources.title: layerSplit is derived by build_stock.py from this stock's linear layer sensitivities over 600-700 nm, not typed in.
KODAK VISION3 500T Color Negative Film 5219 / 7219 / SO-219, Technical Data H-1-5219t: Diffuse rms Granularity Curves (p.4, TI2647C); 48 um aperture
sources.note: Digitised from the figure's grain and density curves (figures/7219_granularity.json); each grain point is taken to density through the same figure's density curve by build_stock.py. Sigma D is the datasheet's dimensionless value (multiply by 1000 for the rms figure).

sources.title: assumption: dye-cloud radius 5 um
sources.note: No primary published dye-cloud radius was found (web searches: dye cloud size colour negative film; dye cloud diameter colour print film granularity). The only figure found is a secondary one, T. Vitale, 'Film Grain, Resolution and Fundamental Film Particles' (2007), which gives colour dye clouds of about 10-15 um (diameter or radius not stated; it also cites a Kodak H-1 micrograph of 1.5-15 um clouds in transparency film). Radius 5 um (10 um diameter, the low end of that range) is used as the starting value for fast colour negative; the fit in M5 treats it as adjustable.
